set_title: Sharp chest pain after a virus: pericardium, myocardium, pleura or chest wall
stem: A 16-year-old boy has had 3 days of sharp left chest pain that lasts seconds and is worse when he twists. He is afebrile. Pressing over the left fourth costochondral junction reproduces the pain. Heart, lungs and ECG are normal.
oneliner: 16M + sharp left chest pain lasting seconds + worse with twisting + reproduced by pressing a costochondral junction + normal heart, lungs, ECG → ?
ask: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

whyNot.B: Pericarditis gives a **rub and diffuse ST elevation**; his ECG and heart exam are normal
whyNot.C: Myocarditis causes **dyspnea or a gallop**; his heart exam is normal
whyNot.D: Pleurodynia follows an enteroviral illness with **fever and paroxysms**; he is afebrile and his pain lasts seconds
whyNot.E: MI at 16 with **normal ECG and pain lasting seconds** reproduced by palpation is not infarction

why: Pain that is **reproduced by pressing the costochondral junction** with a normal heart, lungs and ECG is chest-wall inflammation. Tietze syndrome is the swollen, tender variant.

idea.rule: Chest pain you can reproduce by palpation, normal ECG = costochondritis.

set_title: Bone lesions: myeloma, metastasis or a primary bone tumor
stem: A 15-year-old boy has had 3 weeks of pain and swelling above his right knee. A femoral radiograph shows a lesion centered on the distal metaphysis, with sunburst periosteal new bone and a Codman triangle.
oneliner: 15M + 3 weeks of pain and swelling above the knee + distal femoral metaphyseal lesion + sunburst pattern + Codman triangle → ?
ask: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

whyNot.A: Metastases are rare in teenagers and multiple; he is **15 with a single distal femoral lesion**
whyNot.B: Langerhans cell histiocytosis is a punched-out lytic lesion, often in the skull; his lesion has **a sunburst pattern and Codman triangle**
whyNot.D: Myeloma is a disease of older adults with punched-out lesions; he is **15 with a sunburst lesion**
whyNot.E: Ewing sarcoma lies in the diaphysis with onion-skin layering; his lesion is **metaphyseal with a sunburst pattern**

why: A metaphyseal lesion of the distal femur in an adolescent with a **sunburst pattern and Codman triangle** is osteosarcoma. The tumor makes osteoid, which pushes up the periosteum and radiates new bone outward.

Over 50 years, median about 65
Spine, skull, ribs and pelvis
**Multiple punched-out lytic lesions without a sclerotic rim**
Clonal plasma cells and an M spike; alkaline phosphatase normal
Osteosarcoma
10-20 years (a second peak in older adults with Paget disease)
Metaphysis of long bones: distal femur, proximal tibia
**Sunburst pattern and Codman triangle**
Malignant spindle cells making osteoid; RB1 and TP53 loss
Ewing sarcoma
5-15 years
Diaphysis of long bones (femur) and pelvis; fever mimics osteomyelitis
Lytic, permeative lesion with onion-skin periosteal layers
**Sheets of small round blue cells; t(11;22) EWS-FLI1; CD99; PAS-positive glycogen**
Langerhans cell histiocytosis
Under 15 years (eosinophilic granuloma)
Skull, also ribs, vertebrae and long bones
Punched-out lytic lesion, often in the skull
**CD1a-positive, S-100-positive cells with grooved nuclei and Birbeck granules, plus eosinophils**

idea.rule: Teen with a metaphyseal lesion, sunburst and Codman triangle = osteosarcoma.
also: Distal femur and proximal tibia are the usual sites
RB1 and TP53 mutations raise the risk (retinoblastoma, Li-Fraumeni)
Second peak: Paget disease or radiation

set_title: Bone lesions: myeloma, metastasis or a primary bone tumor
stem: A 14-year-old boy has had 3 weeks of pain and swelling over the left thigh. A radiograph shows a destructive femoral lesion with periosteal new bone. Biopsy shows malignant cells. Ewing sarcoma and osteosarcoma are both being considered.
oneliner: 14M + 3 weeks of thigh pain and swelling + destructive femoral lesion + periosteal new bone + malignant cells on biopsy → Ewing sarcoma or osteosarcoma?
ask: Which single finding favours Ewing sarcoma over osteosarcoma?

options.A: Presentation at the age of 14 years
options.B: Periosteal new bone on the radiograph
options.C: Pain with swelling over the thigh
options.D: Sheets of small round blue cells
options.E: A destructive lesion of the femur

whyNot.A: **Age 14** falls in the range of both
whyNot.B: **Periosteal new bone** occurs in both (onion-skin or sunburst)
whyNot.E: **A destructive femoral lesion** occurs in both

answer: Sheets of small round blue cells
why: Both are bone sarcomas of children and adolescents with a periosteal reaction. Ewing sarcoma is **sheets of small round blue cells with t(11;22) and no osteoid**; osteosarcoma shows pleomorphic spindle cells that make osteoid.
